Findings

Most severe first. Codes are stable identifiers.

warningSharpe fell from 0.74 in-sample to -0.45 out-of-sample (p=0.042).OUT_OF_SAMPLE_DEGRADATION
warningOut-of-sample Sharpe is -0.45.OUT_OF_SAMPLE_SHARPE_NOT_POSITIVE
warningPBO is 72.7%: in that share of train/test splits the best in-sample variant ranked in the bottom half out-of-sample.PROBABILITY_OF_BACKTEST_OVERFITTING
cautionDeflated Sharpe is 64.5%: after accounting for 60 trial(s) there is less than 95% confidence that the true Sharpe is positive.SHARPE_NOT_SIGNIFICANT_AFTER_SELECTION
cautionAbout 49,314 observations are needed to confirm this Sharpe at 95%; the sample has 2,520.TRACK_RECORD_TOO_SHORT
cautionThe 95% bootstrap interval for the annualised Sharpe is [-0.24, 1.06], which includes zero.SHARPE_CI_INCLUDES_ZERO
cautionAlpha of 5.14%/year has a t-statistic of 1.91; performance is not distinguishable from benchmark exposure (beta 0.49).ALPHA_NOT_SIGNIFICANT
infoSkew 0.92, kurtosis 12.4: Sharpe hides tail risk here; read it together with drawdown and the Montecarlo report.FAT_TAILS

Probabilistic Sharpe
Probability that the true Sharpe is above zero given sample length, skew and fat tails.
Deflated Sharpe
The same probability against the best Sharpe expected from 60 skill-less trial(s). Cross-trial dispersion: trials.
Minimum track record
Observations needed for the observed Sharpe to be significant at 95%.
Bootstrap
Stationary, mean block 14, 2000 replicates, seed 0. Newey–West errors for the edge.
Returns
Simple per-period returns, risk-free rate subtracted (rf=0.00%); 252 periods per year.
Not covered
Look-ahead bias, survivorship bias, unrealistic fills and data errors.
